summary: Frontend test of the new 'Change & Release Management' industry template on the demo home '/' and Documentation Portal '/docs'. Found and fixed ONE CRITICAL React runtime crash in TransactionFlow.jsx, then re-ran the full flow. All review_request criteria pass: industry option selectable, hero title/positioning banner/approach cards rendered, custom 6-field form with sample data pre-fills, 10 CRM readiness checks visible, 'Generate Release Readiness Proof' button, all 8 evidence rows correct (workflow-type/release-name/environment/status/checks-passed/transaction-id-as-Release ID/proof-id/timestamp), Release Readiness Certificate with all 7 fields including Ed25519 signature, Cross-Party Consistency + Exception sections hidden, auditor verify with prefilled Proof ID returns Valid + embedded context (Release Name/ID/Environment/Application/CAB Reference/Release Window — no raw data needed), failure-simulation toggle flips status→Not Ready / 9/10 / 90% / 'Blocked — Not Ready'. Regression: Financial Services still shows default 3-field form, no positioning banner / no certificate, Cross-Party Consistency present, proof + auditor verify still work. Docs Portal: 'Industry Use Cases' category present, /docs/use-case-change-release renders doc-content, /docs/releases lists v2.1.0 Change & Release entry.
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED by testing agent: TransactionFlow.jsx imported only { useState } from 'react' but used <React.Fragment> at lines 717/728 to render keyed fragments inside the approach-traditional / approach-pfp arrays. With the new JSX transform React is not auto-injected as a runtime binding, so selecting the Change & Release Management industry threw 'React is not defined' and an error boundary warning ('An error occurred in the <TransactionFlow> component'), crashing the entire demo page. Fix: added `Fragment` to the named imports and replaced <React.Fragment>/</React.Fragment> with <Fragment>/</Fragment>. Suggest E1 add a runtime smoke test or ESLint rule (`react/jsx-no-undef`) so this class of regression is caught at build time.

Minor: positioning banner + approach cards only animate in via conditional render — consider also hiding the small 'Context for compliance checks' helper text under the Industry label when an industry override has its own tagline; today both are shown.

success_rate.frontend: 100% after fix (10/10 review criteria + financial regression + docs portal)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified at viewport 1440x1600 against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL https://pfp-pilot-ready.preview.emergentagent.com. Live /api/demo/issue + /api/demo/verify + /api/demo/artifact calls all succeed (signature surfaced on certificate, auditor verify returns 'Valid Proof — Data Untampered' with full embedded release context). NOTE on auditor-input prefill: the visible evidence-proof-id is the truncated form (e.g. '55c1df2d826bd5e7...0b507e0f') but the auditor input correctly contains the FULL 64-char hex Proof ID — string equality with the truncated display string will fail; assert via substring of the first 16 chars or just call verify and check the returned 'Valid Proof' indicator (that's the user-facing contract). Failure-simulation switch is the first button[role='switch'] on the page in CRM mode.

rca of the issue.bug: Selecting 'Change & Release Management' from the Industry dropdown crashed <TransactionFlow> with 'React is not defined' (caught by React error boundary).
rca of the issue.root_cause: TransactionFlow.jsx uses <React.Fragment key={...}> inside the approach-traditional / approach-pfp maps (lines 717, 728) but the file only imports { useState } from 'react' — React itself is not bound at runtime under the new JSX transform.
rca of the issue.reproduction: 1) Open '/'  2) Click [data-testid=industry-select-trigger]  3) Click [data-testid=industry-option-change_release]  → page goes blank / hero unreachable; console shows PAGE ERROR: React is not defined and a <TransactionFlow> error boundary warning.
rca of the issue.mitigation_applied: Replaced default-React access with a named import: `import { useState, Fragment } from 'react'` and `<React.Fragment>` → `<Fragment>` (2 occurrences). Hot reload picked up the change; full CRM + regression + docs flows now pass.
